author: Kai Moreno
title: SIEM connector for metrics and traces (not platform events)
content:
# Purpose
Customers sometimes want Prometheus remote-write, OTLP traces, or Grafana Cloud to see latency and error rates. That is a metrics and traces connector. It is not the same as copying platform event records.

# When to use
The customer mentions dashboards, p95, span IDs, Grafana, Datadog, or 'our observability stack'. They are talking about signals, not a compliance archive.

# Intake
Collect sink type (Datadog / Grafana / OTLP), region of the sink, and whether they already have a Dedicated scrape endpoint. Hosted customers get a read-only metrics remote-write. Dedicated customers scrape from their own Prometheus.

# Priority and routing
Treat this as a how-to: priority P4, leave the ticket with Support, first response from the SLA table for P4. Do not escalate. Do not assign Eng Platform unless the Dedicated scrape endpoint is broken.

# What Support does
Send the public docs for metrics remote-write. Confirm they are not asking for a compliance archive. If they are, stop and use the customer-managed export SOP instead.

# Guardrails
Never promise that metrics include prompt text or request bodies. Metrics are counters, histograms, and resource attributes only.

# Common mix-up
A customer who says 'put the logs in our bucket for ISO' is not this page. This page is dashboards. The other request is a compliance archive and has its own SOP.

# Related
Dedicated scrape endpoint runbook. Hosted metrics remote-write. Do not file these as security incidents.
